notes: Current USMLE communication content supports responding to patient emotion and difficult encounters.
NCBI Clinical Methods supports reflection/explicit acknowledgment of anger as an effective first intervention before argument, justification, or problem solving.

exact_locator_notes: USMLE Content Outline — current relevant system/competency section.

blueprint.system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A nonviolent but explicitly angry patient should first have the emotion acknowledged and reflected; explanation of the delay can follow once the patient feels heard.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Immediate justification, normalization, premature limit-setting, or rescheduling without acknowledgment fails to address the expressed emotion first.
